intro: Saturday June 20. US markets reopen Monday June 22 — the week's most consequential session. The weekend setup is more constructive than Thursday evening: DXY declined to ~100.23 on weekend FX (was 100.79 Thursday), IBIT outflow streak ended with $86M net inflows led by BlackRock, BTC is tracking a third consecutive UTC close above the $63,500 stop, and SK Hynix officially shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples. The ideas below are calibrated for the June 22 open. Three scenarios diverge from that session: (A) DXY closes below 100 on June 22 → NVDA conditional-add activates (all three gates clear), BTC conviction upgrades, risk-on recovery accelerates; (B) DXY holds above 100 → NVDA add suspended, hold defensive posture until Annual Meeting June 24; (C) 30Y breaks above 5.00% → STEP_ASIDE across high-multiple names, reduce equity exposure broadly. The week's primary catalyst beyond June 22 is the NVDA Annual Meeting June 24 (Jensen Huang's first post-FOMC public appearance) and Micron Q3 earnings (first post-FOMC semiconductor demand read-through).

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: Official HBM4E sample shipment confirmed (SK Hynix Newsroom) — unconditional add on any KOSPI pullback to ₩2,688,000–₩2,750,000 before June 23 KOSPI open.
ideas.why: SK Hynix's official Newsroom confirmed shipment of 12-layer HBM4E samples to major AI customers (48GB capacity, 16Gbps per pin, 20%+ power efficiency improvement). This is the product-generation confirmation that justifies all 38 analysts revising their PTs from the outdated ₩2,690,000 consensus. The market cap briefly crossed ₩2,000T at the June 19 intraday ATH (₩2,891,000). A potential ₩75T (~$48B) buyback program is being reported. Micron Q3 earnings this week are a read-through catalyst: a MU beat-and-raise with strong HBM demand commentary will gap SK Hynix higher on June 23 KOSPI open. The US macro (DXY declining to 100.23) is easing the USD/KRW FX headwind on the ~54% foreign-owned float.
ideas.trigger: Any KOSPI session on June 23 pulling back to ₩2,688,000–₩2,750,000 (June 19 session floor zone) → add immediately; stop raised to ₩2,540,000. Also: if Goldman Sachs or BofA issue a ₩3.0M+ PT note before June 23 KOSPI open, add at any price on the open — that PT revision is the next institutional accumulation wave trigger.
ideas.risk: Micron Q3 earnings miss on AI memory (HBM demand weaker than expected) — direct read-through negative for SK Hynix before June 23 KOSPI; or Samsung announces a specific NVIDIA HBM4E qualification win before SK Hynix completes its own qualification.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: June 22 is the conditional-add trigger day — DXY at 100.23 weekend puts all three gates within a single session of clearing simultaneously for the first time since June 13.
ideas.why: DXY declined to ~100.23 on weekend FX (from 100.79 Thursday) — the single remaining conditional-add gate is 23 bps away. VIX gate CLEARED (~16.78). SPX gate CLEARED (7,500.58). If DXY closes below 100.00 on June 22, all three gates clear simultaneously and the $205–$215 add executes at the first confirmed-gate close. NVDA's last official close of $208.82 (June 18) is the first close above the 50-DMA since the FOMC dump — the technical recovery confirmation is intact. SK Hynix's official HBM4E confirmation (supplier through 2030) removes supply-chain execution risk from NVDA's Vera Rubin timeline. Annual Meeting June 24 is the override: Jensen Huang's first post-FOMC public commentary is the event that can trigger the add regardless of gate status.
ideas.trigger: June 22 session close: DXY below 100.00 AND VIX below 17 on the same session → execute add at $205–$215, stop $195. If DXY holds above 100: hold existing, wait for Annual Meeting June 24. Annual Meeting June 24: Jensen explicitly bullish on AI capex in hawkish rate environment → add regardless of gate status.
ideas.risk: DXY reverses the weekend decline on June 22 open (Warsh hawkish Fed speech, strong PMI data); 30Y breaks above 5.00% before June 22 close — both scenarios keep the conditional add suspended.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: IBIT outflow streak ended — conviction upgraded to medium; hold through June 22 ETF flow confirmation, size-up on second consecutive IBIT inflow day.
ideas.why: Two major positive developments since June 19 brief: (1) IBIT outflow streak ended — BlackRock's IBIT led $86M in net Bitcoin ETF inflows (bitcoin.com), reversing the institutional selling signal; (2) BTC is tracking a third consecutive UTC close above the $63,500 stop at $63,711 as of 11:01 UTC. The June 20 Deribit weekly expiry cleared Friday, removing the $64,000 dealer delta-hedge selling overhang. DXY declining to ~100.23 improves the macro regime for BTC (BTC/DXY inverse correlation). The double-bottom at $62,255–$62,313 (June 18 and June 19 lows) is intact with two tests and two holds. June 22 US session is the first post-holiday ETF flow print — a second consecutive IBIT inflow day confirms the reversal is institutional, not a one-day anomaly.
ideas.trigger: June 20 UTC midnight close above $63,500 (on track) + June 22 IBIT flow data showing second consecutive net inflow day → upgrade to medium-high conviction, add 20–25% position size at $63,500–$65,000. Alternative: BTC closes above $65,000 on June 22 US session close → double-bottom confirmed, target $67,000.
ideas.risk: BTC closes below $63,500 on June 20 UTC midnight → stop clock re-activates; DXY reverses above 101 on June 22 open; June 22 IBIT flow shows resumed outflows (false reversal) — reduce back to hold at low conviction.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Step aside; monitor June 22 opening price at $165–$175 for stabilization watch; June 20 weekly options cleared; DXY improving is the most constructive weekend development.
ideas.why: The $185 daily close stop triggered at $174.90 on June 18 — framework requires exit. June 20 weekly options expiry has now CLEARED (the $195 max-pain gamma headwind expired). DXY declining to 100.23 (from 100.79 Thursday) reduces the rate-discount compression on the 84x revenue multiple — most constructive macro for SPCX since the June 18 stop trigger. Analyst consensus: 6 buy / 1 sell, average PT $187.80 (above current $174.90). The June 22 open at $165–$175 with recovering volume (>150M shares) initiates the 3–5 session stabilization watch; two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume is the re-entry trigger.
ideas.trigger: June 22 open: SPCX $165–$175 AND volume >150M shares → begin stabilization watch (do not buy yet); two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume = re-entry with stop $165 and July put hedge. SPCX opens below $165 → correction extending, wait for $150–$160.
ideas.risk: DXY reverses above 101 on June 22 open → multiple compression resumes; MSCI passive bid exhausted (Day 10+ post-IPO) leaving retail as marginal buyer; September 2 earnings uncertainty remains elevated.

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: Best post-FOMC dip buy in megacap tech — IBIT inflows + DXY declining signal risk-on recovery; entry at $545–$560 on June 22 open.
ideas.why: Meta fell -5.44% on June 17 — the largest FOMC-session loss among megacaps. But Meta's fundamentals are the cleanest in big tech: AI capex funded entirely from operations, strong ad revenue acceleration, no debt, and the cheapest forward multiple in the Magnificent-7 post-selloff. The weekend developments (IBIT inflows ended, DXY declining) are precisely the macro signals that preceded the last three post-FOMC megacap recoveries. META's self-funded AI model (no external debt, no rate sensitivity) makes it the most pure-equity play on FOMC-shock recovery. The IBIT inflows signal returning institutional risk appetite — META is the first destination for that capital in megacap tech.
ideas.trigger: June 22 open: VIX stays below 18 (on track at 16.78 weekend) AND DXY shows further decline from 100.23 → buy META at $545–$560; stop $530 daily close. If DXY reverses above 101 on June 22 open: stand aside on META until macro stabilizes.
ideas.risk: 30Y Treasury tests 5.00% → multiple compression accelerates across all long-duration growth assets; June 22-26 Warsh Fed speaker reaffirms rate-hike probability above 40%; AI regulatory headlines (antitrust, data privacy).

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: Q3 earnings read-through to AI memory demand — beat-and-raise with strong HBM commentary is the week's top semiconductor catalyst.
ideas.why: Micron reports Q3 fiscal year 2026 earnings during the week of June 22-25 — the first major post-FOMC semiconductor demand print. MU holds 21% global HBM market share and is the most direct US-listed proxy for the AI memory cycle. If MU beats revenue consensus and guides above expectations with strong HBM commentary (demand accelerating, ASPs holding), it is a direct read-through positive for NVDA (AI demand intact) and for SK Hynix (global HBM leader). Post-FOMC selloff gave MU a better entry than pre-FOMC: AI memory demand is not rate-sensitive and the FOMC selloff represents mispriced fundamentals, not a change in the AI capex cycle.
ideas.trigger: Ahead of earnings: buy MU at $95–$105 with stop at $90 daily close; position for beat-and-raise. Post-earnings: if MU beats and guides above consensus → hold for post-earnings momentum; if MU misses or guides down → exit immediately, reassess NVDA and SK Hynix long theses.
ideas.risk: MU warns on HBM demand (AI capex cycle digestion pause); FOMC rate path uncertainty creating enterprise IT budget pressure on cloud customers; Samsung HBM market-share gains accelerating faster than MU's consensus model.

ideas.name: SPDR Energy Select Sector ETF
ideas.idea: Iran ceasefire in effect — Hormuz reopening; H2 2026 earnings estimate cuts not yet in sell-side numbers; DXY declining adds commodity-equity headwind.
ideas.why: The Iran ceasefire formal signing in Switzerland (June 19) confirmed the Hormuz reopening timeline (30 days for mine-clearance, commercial traffic already flowing). Brent at ~$79 is structurally below the $87–90 embedded in H2 2026 energy equity models — sell-side analysts have not yet revised H2 estimates down by the required 8–12%. DXY declining to 100.23 (soft dollar = slightly stronger oil in local currency terms) may produce a brief Brent bounce toward $82–84 on mine-clearance timeline speculation — use any such bounce as the better short entry size-up opportunity. The Warsh hawkish FOMC compounds the XLE short: risk-off + commodity demand uncertainty + oil supply increase is a triple headwind for energy equities.
ideas.trigger: June 22: if XLE opens at $53–$56 with Brent below $82 → initiate or add to short; any Brent bounce to $82–$84 on Hormuz timeline delays is the premium short entry. Cover only if Brent closes above $90 on two consecutive sessions.
ideas.risk: Iran deal collapses; Hormuz clearance delayed beyond 60 days; OPEC+ announces unexpected production cuts; Brent spikes above $90 on supply shock.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: Post-FOMC dip at $375–$390 — Azure AI monetization compounds regardless of rate path; least rate-sensitive megacap AI play.
ideas.why: Microsoft fell ~3.79% on June 17 FOMC-day. At ~$378, Azure AI monetization and Copilot attach rates are compounding on a subscription-revenue model that is largely rate-insensitive (contracted enterprise bookings). The IBIT outflows ending and DXY declining signal improving risk appetite — MSFT is the safest entry in the recovery trade for investors who want exposure without the tail risk of NVDA (gate-dependent) or BTC (stop-framework). MSFT's recurring-revenue model provides the clearest P/E support in the Mag-7 at current levels.
ideas.trigger: VIX stays below 18 on June 22 AND MSFT holds $375 support → buy at $375–$390, stop $368 daily close.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-Azure-revenue monetization lag extends; SPCX AI narrative continues pulling growth capital from 'mature AI' incumbents; 30Y above 5.00% compresses all growth multiples.
